title: Header says mark exits 2 for an unknown pass; the code exits 1
detail: The MARK paragraph says 'A pass that is out of order, already done or unknown exits 2 with the file untouched'. Line 170 rejects an unknown --pass with bad() (KitExit 1), and the unit test at test/kit-unslop-ordered-redline-passes.test.js:164 pins exit 1. A probe confirmed it: `mark --state p.json --pass sparkle` exits 1. A caller who branches on the documented exit codes (2 = refusal and retry with the next pass, 1 = broken input) gets the wrong branch. The same text is in .claude/helpers/kit/redline-passes.js:24.
fix_hint: Change the header in both copies to 'A pass that is out of order or already done exits 2; an unknown pass id exits 1'. That matches the code and the test.

title: next/remaining depend on where the first problem sits, so `next` can name a pass already listed as done
detail: evaluate stops at the first problem (line 98) and builds `remaining` only from the ids it saw before that point. For {"done":["spacing","bogus","color"]} it returns next=color and keeps color in `remaining`, although color is in `done`. The header (line 13) says `next` 'still names the first pass of the plan that is not done'. The answer is arguably the right advice, but it contradicts the stated rule. The `fix` text 'Redo the passes out of order' also points at the wrong pass for unknown or repeated ids.
fix_hint: Either reword the header: on a problem, `next` is the first plan pass after the last in-order prefix. Or compute `next` from the in-order prefix explicitly and word `fix` for each problem kind.

title: Concurrent-mark test does not check why the losers failed
detail: 'serialises concurrent marks' asserts only that at least one mark succeeded and that the file holds an in-order prefix. A loser that failed with a lock timeout or a lost-lock KitExit 1 would also pass the test, although the behaviour the spec needs is a refusal (exit 2).
fix_hint: Also assert that every rejected result is a KitExit with code 2, and that done.length equals the number of fulfilled results.

title: next signature line omits batch, reminder and exit
detail: The return shape documented for `next` is { next, done, remaining, ok, problem?, fix? }. The code can also add `batch` and `reminder` (--all-at-once) and `exit: 2` (--strict). The ALL AT ONCE and STATE paragraphs describe these, but the signature line, which readers scan first, does not.
fix_hint: Extend the line to { next, done, remaining, ok, problem?, fix?, batch?, reminder?, exit? } in both copies.

title: from-brief on real assume output prefills product from assumed placeholders and marks it done
detail: The header says from-brief accepts design-brief's assume output ({ kind, brief }). Real assume output always fills every field, using the kind's default text for any answer that is missing, and lists those defaults in `assumptions`. fromBrief ignores `assumptions`, so offer and audience always look answered. Probe: `echo '{"kind":"ui","answers":{}}' | cli.js design-brief assume | cli.js direction from-brief` returns product.text "one clear job for the screen, taken from the request, for a regular user on desktop and phone, so the layout is responsive and moderately dense." with todo: false and prefilled: ["product"]. The same happens when only the offer was given: the audience becomes the default string. So the skeleton presents generic filler as the user's product line and tells them it needs no answer, which defeats the verb's purpose on a documented input. The unit test 'accepts the assume output shape' uses a made-up { kind, brief: { offer } } that real assume never produces, which is why the bug was missed.
fix_hint: When the input has `brief`, treat each field named in `assumptions[].field` as missing (do not prefill offer or audience from it, set todo: true and add a note). Add a test that pipes real `assume()` output (from design-brief.js) through fromBrief, with no answers and with offer only.

title: JSON moments array is re-split on 'and' and commas, so two moments count as three
detail: fromJson joins a moments array with '; ' and judge() then counts items() on the joined string. items() also splits on ',', 'and', '&' and '+', so a moment written as an array element is split again. Probe: moments ["the total and subtotal row", "the print button"] gives too_many_moments (counted as 3) even though the user gave exactly two places. The array form is the one input where the count is known for certain, yet it gets the heuristic's false positives, and with --strict it exits 2.
fix_hint: Keep the array length from fromJson (for example store values.__count.moments = v.length) and use it for the too_many_moments check instead of items(); add a test with an array element that contains 'and'.

title: On an out-of-order state, remaining and --all-at-once batch silently drop the misplaced pass
detail: evaluate() adds the offending id to `seen` before the loop stops, and `remaining` is IDS minus `seen`. For done=["spacing","motion"] (probed via cli.js) `next --all-at-once` returns ok=false and remaining/batch = color..visuals, with no motion. The fix text tells the user to redo the passes in plan order, but the list it hands back as 'the whole remaining list' leaves out a pass that still has to be applied in order. An agent that follows the batch never does motion. The same happens with plain `next`: `remaining` names 7 passes instead of 8. No test covers remaining or batch on a broken state.
fix_hint: Build `remaining` from the in-order prefix only (IDS.slice(prefixLength)), or skip seen.add for the offending id when the problem is 'order'. Add a test that done=["spacing","motion"] gives remaining/batch = IDS.slice(1).

title: parseFlags looks flags up on a plain object, so Object.prototype names are accepted as flags
detail: `spec[a]` finds inherited members: `next toString x`, `next constructor x` or `mark ... valueOf y` find a truthy function, take the next argument as its value and exit 0 instead of the documented exit 1 'unexpected argument' (`next toString x` probed: exit 0).
fix_hint: Use Object.hasOwn(spec, a) (or a Map / Object.create(null) spec) before reading kind.

title: Header says every bad `done` is reported by next as ok=false, but non-string ids exit 1
detail: STATE says '`done` must be an array of pass ids ...; anything else is reported by `next` as ok=false with a `problem` (an unknown id, ...)'. readState throws exit 1 for {"done":[1]} before evaluate runs (the test 'nums.json' expects that), so a non-string entry is not an ok=false advisory answer. The unknown-id branch in evaluate for non-strings cannot be reached through run.
fix_hint: Say in the header that a non-string entry (like a missing `done`) exits 1, or drop the readState check and let evaluate report it as unknown.

title: A refused mark still creates the state file's folder
detail: withStateLock creates the parent folder before the order check runs, so `mark --state sub/x.json --pass color` exits 2 ('file untouched') and leaves an empty `sub/` directory behind (probed). Small, but it contradicts 'refusal leaves things untouched' for a new path.
fix_hint: Check the order against a lock-free read first and refuse before taking the lock, then re-check inside the lock; or document that the folder is created.

title: JSON array of blank strings passes as a present field instead of missing
detail: fromJson joins array elements with '; ' before checkFields trims, so {"moments": [" ", ""]} becomes text ';' (present: true, no problems) and ["","",""," "] becomes '; ; ;' with count 0. The missing check never fires, so with the other four fields valid, check returns ok: true and --strict exits 0 for an empty moments line (probed via cli.js direction check). The same applies to any field given as an array. The .claude/helpers copy has the same code. No test covers it.
fix_hint: Drop blank elements before joining (v.map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean).join('; ')) so an all-blank array gives '' and reports missing; add a test for moments: [' ', ''].

title: Arrays are accepted for every field, but the docs and error message say only moments
detail: The array branch has no id === 'moments' guard, so {"character": ["patient"]} is accepted and joined, yet the header says 'moments may be an array of strings' and line 179's error offers the array form only for moments. A wrong-shaped input for other fields is accepted without an error.
fix_hint: Limit the array branch to id === 'moments', or document that every field accepts an array of strings.

title: Exact duplicate JSON keys: last one wins silently, while text input says first wins and flags it
detail: JSON.parse keeps the last of {"product":"a","product":"b"} (probed: text 'b', no problem), and the 'given more than once' guard at line 174 only catches case variants. The markdown path reports duplicate_field and keeps the first. So the same mistake behaves differently depending on the input format.
fix_hint: Document that duplicate JSON keys are last-wins, or detect exact repeats (for example with a reviver or a light key scan) and report duplicate_field.

title: Non-object JSON (null, an array) on check is read as markdown and reported as five missing fields
detail: Only a leading '{' routes to fromJson, so a JSON file containing null or ["Product: a"] goes to parseText and returns ok:false with five 'missing' problems and exit 0. The 'direction JSON must be an object' error in fromJson can never be reached from the CLI. This follows the documented sniffing rule, but the user gets a misleading message instead of a clear input error.
fix_hint: Also treat a leading '[' (or text that parses as JSON) as JSON, so fromJson's object error is shown with exit 1.

title: JSX input: code after the first tag is scanned as visible copy
detail:
visibleText (jsx) blanks only the text before the first TAG_RE match. After that, seg() blanks only brace groups that open and close inside one tag-to-tag segment and nest at most two levels deep. A function body broken up by JSX tags, top-level statements, or a TS generic (useState, forwardRef, Array, all matched as tags) therefore reaches the copy detectors as raw code. Probe: a plain two-component .jsx file (Header returns

Projects

; Footer has `const port = 1234;` and `throw new Error('year is required!')`) gives fake-data on line 6 and exclamation-marks on line 7, and `scan --strict --file b.jsx` exits 2. A shadcn-style forwardRef Button gives the same false hits. The header promises that copy signs read visible text only, and the workflows block on --strict, so ordinary component files fail the gate because of their code.
fix_hint: For jsx, take visible text only from JSX children: the text between a tag's '>' and the next '<' or '{' while inside an element, with a depth count of open and close tags. Blank everything outside elements and every {...} expression. Do not treat a '<Ident...>' that follows an identifier or '(' as a tag. Add a regression test with two components, a TS generic and an Error('...!') string, and assert zero copy hits.

title: Markdown fence closing ignores fence length and info string
detail:
maskCode closes a fence on any line that starts with three or more of the same fence character. CommonMark requires the closing fence to be at least as long as the opener and to carry no info string. So a ````md block that shows a ```js example ends at the inner ```, and a line '```js' inside a block is taken as a close. Code after that point is then scanned as prose. Probe: '# T

```js
const a = "x!";
```js
Welcome back!
```' on stdin reports greeting-headline and exclamation-marks on line 6, which is inside the code block. Docs that show markdown or code samples are a normal input for this verb.
fix_hint: Record the opener's character and length. Close only on a line matching ^ {0,3}(char){len,}[ \t]*$. Add a nested-fence test.

title: A README that opens with an HTML block is sniffed as html, so its fenced code is scanned
detail:
sniff returns md only when the text does not start with '<' (`!/^<[a-z]/i.test(t)`). Many READMEs open with a centred logo block such as

and then use # headings. Those are sniffed as html, and --file ignores the .md extension by design, so the markdown masking (fences, inline code) never runs. Probe: such a README.md with a ```sh fence containing echo "done!" and inline `x!` gives format html and exclamation-marks hits on lines 8 and 11, both of which are code. Without --format md the user gets wrong hits, and --strict blocks on them.
fix_hint:
Let a leading run of HTML block lines fall through to the markdown check. For example, test the md signals on the text with leading HTML blocks stripped, or count a line-start '# ' heading or fence anywhere in the text as md even when the text opens with a tag. Add a test for a README that starts with a logo

.

title: Product name matched as a substring, not a word
detail:
templateTest builds `new RegExp(esc(nm), 'gi')` with no word boundaries, so a short product name counts wherever it appears inside another word. Probe: `template-test --name Arc` on `

Search everything faster. Streamline your workflow.

` returns name_found: true, occurrences: 1, but the page never names Arc (the match is the 'arc' in 'Search'). The replacement also splits the host word ('se\u0002h'), which leaves non-generic fragments ('se', 'h') behind and can pull a generic sentence out of the generic count. Real names like Arc, Box (inbox), Loom (bloom), Linear (nonlinear) and Notion (notional) give a false name_found or a lower generic_ratio, and the result also feeds check --name --strict.
fix_hint: Match on word boundaries that work for any name, e.g. `new RegExp('(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])' + esc(nm) + '(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])', 'giu')`, and add a test where the name appears only inside another word.

title: sniff differs from landing-sections and has no --format override
detail:
The header says sections are found 'by landing-sections' detection', but this verb uses its own sniff, and that sniff does not skip the ``, `{%...%}` and `{#...#}` prologs that landing-sections' sniff skips, so the same file gets a different type in each verb. Probe: a Jinja page starting with `{% extends "base.html" %}` whose after version drops `` is sniffed as md, so check reports no violations and pass: true. A GitHub-style README that starts with `

` is sniffed as html, so its markdown headings and links are never read: probe r1.md -> r2.md swapped `## Install`/`## Usage` and removed `[docs](https://x.y/docs)`, and check still returned violations: [] and pass: true, even under --strict. landing-sections offers `--format md|html` for this case; template-test and check offer no override.
fix_hint: Export landing-sections' sniff and reuse it (one detector for both verbs), and accept `--format md|html` on template-test and `--before-format/--after-format` (or one --format) on check, with a test for each misdetected case.

title: Ordered-list markers reported as invented data
detail: visibleMarkdown strips bullet markers (`[ \t>#*+-]`) but not ordered-list markers (`1.`, `2)`), so the marker digits stay in the visible copy and NUM matches them. Probe: changing a `- Open the file / - Save it` list to `1. Open the file / 2. Save it` gives two invented-data violations ("1", "2"), which makes --strict exit 2. The same change in HTML (ul -> ol) is not flagged, so md and html input disagree.
fix_hint: Also strip `^\s*\d{1,9}[.)][ \t]+` from each line in visibleMarkdown, and add a test.

title: lineOf rescans from the start for every match (quadratic)
detail: lineOf counts newlines from index 0 on every call, and fieldNames, linkTargets, firstLines and headings call it once per distinct match, so check runs in O(size x matches). Probe: a 900 KB before page with 20k links and 20k fields takes 5.3 s; at the documented 8 MiB cap it would take minutes. Normal pages are small, so this is low.
fix_hint: Build a sorted array of newline offsets once per text and binary-search it, or count lines while scanning matches in order.

title: "Change the direction" leaves an earlier confirmation in place, so the gate still opens
detail: confirm with --choice 'Change the direction' throws exit 2 and writes nothing, but it does not remove or overwrite a state file that an earlier confirm wrote. Probe: confirm --state st.json --grade heavy (exit 0), then confirm --state st.json --grade heavy --choice 'Change the direction' (exit 2, 'nothing recorded'), then gate --state st.json exits 0 with confirmed:true. When the state file is reused, for example after a re-grade in the same run or a second run on the same stream, the stop-before-edit gate lets edits through even though the user just said no. That is the one thing the gate exists to stop. The gate (lines 249-258) also never ties a confirmation to a particular grade run, so any old record passes. No test covers the confirm-then-refuse sequence.
fix_hint: On 'Change the direction', atomically write { confirmed: false, choice, at } over the state file (or rm it) before exiting 2, and add a test: confirm Go, confirm Change, gate must exit 2.

title: "Only refine, keep the design" is recorded under the original grade, so the gate reports heavy/light
detail: confirm --grade heavy --choice 'Only refine, keep the design' writes grade: 'heavy', and gate returns { confirmed: true, grade: 'heavy', choice: 'Only refine, keep the design' } (probed). A caller that branches on gate's `grade` will run the full redline passes or polish mode even though the user chose to keep the design. The test at test/kit-unslop-triage-and-refine-only-gate.test.js:191 makes this the expected behaviour (grade light plus Only refine) and checks only `choice`.
fix_hint: When choice is 'Only refine, keep the design', record grade 'refine-only' (keep the graded value as e.g. `graded`), and assert gate's grade is 'refine-only' in that test.

title: validateAudit accepts counts and total that contradict hits, and grade then gives a wrong result
detail: The validator checks each field's type but never checks that total === hits.length or that counts[g] equals the number of hits in group g. grade() decides from counts/total while plan() lists hits, so an inconsistent input (hand-edited, or merged from several files' scans) is graded silently and wrongly. Probe: the real slop-audit output for a 6-hit screen with counts and total zeroed grades 'refine-only', 'no slop signs found', and still lists hits as refinements. With hits emptied and counts left in place it grades 'heavy' and has no fixes. The header promises 'A wrong shape exits 1 with the field named'.
fix_hint: After the field checks, throw bad('audit.total: must equal hits.length') and bad(`audit.counts.${g}: must equal the hits in group ${g}`) when they disagree; add two validateAudit cases.

title: Unit tests drive only the fake `stdin`, never the `stdinBytes` path the CLI uses, nor the cap on --file
detail: The io() fake passes only `stdin`, so the `io.stdinBytes` branch at slop-triage.js:238, which is the one the real CLI takes, runs only in the packaged happy path. The 8 MiB cap is tested only through stdin (line 112). The --file read at line 236 has its own cap in openRegular, with no test. The BOM test (line 123) also covers stdin only. No test feeds real `slop-audit scan --strict` output, which carries an extra `exit` key.
fix_hint: Add stdinBytes to the fake io (or a second io), plus a test that writes a >8 MiB file and runs --file on it, a BOM test via --file, and a fixture of real scan --strict output.

title: refine-only slice to REFINE_MAX_EDITS can never take effect; the no-slop case offers no refinements
detail: refine-only allows at most REFINE_MAX_HITS (2) hits, so hits.slice(0, REFINE_MAX_EDITS = 3) never cuts anything, and the test at line 84 (`<= 3` on 2 hits) passes without the cap being needed. With total 0, refinements is [], but the brief asks for two or three small refinements with exact values when there is no slop. The plan's steps say so only in prose.
fix_hint: Drop the dead slice (or assert exact lengths), and say plainly in the plan or note that with zero hits the agent supplies the 2-3 refinements itself.

title: words() rgb/hsl regex is quadratic: a 400 KB Signature line takes 35 s, 8 MiB effectively hangs
detail: words() runs /\b(?:rgba?|hsla?)\([^)]*\)/g over the whole signature/world text (onlyFrom, judge lines 115-116). For every 'rgb(' / 'hsl(' with no closing ')' the [^)]* scans to the end of the string before failing, so the cost is O(occurrences x length). Probe: 'Signature: ' + 'rgb('.repeat(100000) (400 KB) took 35 s of CPU in `direction check --file`; at the documented 8 MiB cap (about 2M occurrences) the run is about 400x longer, i.e. hours, with no output. The field text is not length-capped before judge (too_long only reports), so the 8 MiB input guard does not bound the work. On a slow or older machine the threshold for a noticeable stall is much lower. Same code in src/lib/kit/direction.js line 523.
fix_hint: Bound the match: use [^)]{0,64} (or [^()]*\) with a length cap), or skip onlyFrom/words when text.length > MAX_FIELD (it is already a too_long problem); add a test that a 1 MiB 'rgb(' signature finishes quickly.

title: UTF-16 input (Windows PowerShell 5.1 redirect default) is reported as 'looks binary' with no encoding hint
detail: readText only strips a UTF-8 BOM and then refuses any NUL. A direction file written with Windows PowerShell 5.1 `>` / Out-File is UTF-16LE with an FF FE BOM, so it is refused as 'input looks binary (contains NUL bytes)'. Exit 1 is safe, but the message sends the user looking for a corrupt file instead of telling them to save as UTF-8. Probe: iconv -t utf-16le of a valid Product/Character block gives exit 1 'input looks binary'. Same code in src/lib/kit/direction.js line 688.
fix_hint: Detect a leading FF FE / FE FF BOM and either decode it (buf.toString('utf16le')) or say 'input is UTF-16; save it as UTF-8'.

title: --accent #000000 (light) or #ffffff (dark) gives a hover equal to the base
detail: hover is oklchToRgb(clamp01(ao.L +/- 0.06), ...). For a black accent in light mode L is already 0, and for a white accent in dark mode L is already 1, so the clamp leaves L unchanged and --color-accent-hover is the same colour as --color-accent (probed: emit --accent '#000000' gives base #000000, hover #000000; emit --accent '#ffffff' --mode dark gives base #ffffff, hover #ffffff). Black and white are real brand accents for monochrome brands, and the sheet then has no visible hover state. Tests only use #e11d48.
fix_hint: When the shifted L hits the clamp (or the result equals the base), move L the other way instead, and add a test with --accent #000000 and --accent #ffffff --mode dark asserting hover !== base.

title: A grey --accent sets the ramp hue from rounding noise
detail: With only --accent given, the ramp hue is rgbToOklch(accent).h. For an achromatic accent (#ffffff, #808080) C is about 0 and h comes from atan2 of float noise: both probe to hue 89.9, so a monochrome brand gets a yellow-tinted ramp it never asked for; #000000 gives 0 (reddish). The header promises 'the hue of --accent', which a grey does not have.
fix_hint: If the accent's OKLCH chroma is below a small threshold (e.g. 0.02), fall back to DEFAULT_HUE for the ramp, and note it in notes.

title: --hue 359.95 to 359.99 is accepted and reported as hue 360
detail: The --hue check accepts any value below 360, then emit rounds to one decimal, so --hue 359.99 prints "hue": 360 and a 'hue 360' css header, outside the documented 0-359 range.
fix_hint: Take the rounded value modulo 360 (h = (Math.round(h * 10) / 10) % 360).

title: OFF_GRID_SPACING misses px values glued to !important
detail: Spacing tokens are split on whitespace and matched with /^(-?\d*\.?\d+)px$/, so 'margin:5px!important' (the minified form) is never flagged, while 'padding:6px !important' is (probed). font-weight strips !important first, so the two rules disagree on the same input.
fix_hint: Strip a trailing \s*!important from value before splitting, as the font-weight branch already does.

title: The 8 MiB cap is tested on stdin only, not on --file
detail: openRegular has its own read loop and its own 'larger than 8 MiB' check (design-tokens.js lines 381-388), but no unit or packaged test passes an oversize file with --file; both oversize tests go through stdin. The unit io helper also never supplies stdinBytes, so the byte path the real CLI uses runs only in the packaged test.
fix_hint: In 'reads --file and matches stdin', write a MAX_BYTES + 1 file and assert exit 1, plus one exactly MAX_BYTES file that is accepted.

title: An empty --file gets the stdin hint
detail: check --file e.css on an empty or whitespace-only file fails with 'no input: pass CSS on stdin or --file', which reads as if --file was not given at all, and does not name the file.
fix_hint: When f.file is set, say '<path> is empty' instead.

title: A markdown doc whose code sample contains className= is sniffed as jsx, and its prose is never scanned
detail:
sniff tests the jsx signals (` className\s*=`, `function Foo(`, `=> (<`) anywhere in the text, before the markdown check. So a README or docs page for a React component, a normal input for this verb, gets sniffed as jsx when a fenced example contains className=. jsxVisible then treats the prose as code and blanks it, and the markdown fence masking never runs. Probe: '# My Button

Welcome back! This is a revolutionary button.

```jsx
<Button className="px-4">Click me!</Button>
```' via --file README.md gives format jsx and 0 hits. With --format md the same file gives greeting-headline, exclamation-marks and hype-words on line 3. The scan passes silently under --strict. This is the same class of bug as the r1 README-as-html sniff, which was fixed only for a leading HTML block.
fix_hint: Run the markdown signals before the jsx signals when the text does not start with import/export, or test the jsx signals on the text with fenced blocks and inline code removed. Add a test for a README with a ```jsx fence containing className=.

title: A TSX generic arrow <T extends X>(...) is parsed as a JSX element, so the code after it is read as copy
detail: tagStartsAt accepts '<' after '=', and parseElement accepts `<T extends unknown>` as an element named T with two boolean attributes. Everything after the '>' is then shown as text children up to the next '<' or '{', so top-level code reaches the copy detectors. `<T extends ...>` is the usual way to write a generic arrow in a .tsx file. Probe: g.tsx with `const identity = <T extends unknown>(x: T): T => x;` followed by `const port = 1234;` and `throw new Error('year is required!');` gives fake-data on line 3 and exclamation-marks on line 4, and --strict would exit 2. The r1 regression tests cover useState<string> and forwardRef<...> but not this form.
fix_hint: In tagStartsAt or parseElement, reject a candidate when the name is followed by `extends` and the closing '>' is followed by '(' (a type-parameter list). Add this case to the TS-generics regression test.

title: jsx scanner has no regex-literal handling, so a backtick in a regex swallows the rest of the file
detail:
scanCode treats every quote as the start of a string. A regex literal holding a backtick, such as `const re = /`/;`, opens a template string in skipString that runs to the end of the file. Nothing after it is read: `

Welcome back!

` on the next line gives 0 hits, a silent false negative. A regex holding '{' or '}' inside a {expression} also shifts the brace depth. This is rare in component files.
fix_hint: In scanCode, when '/' follows an operator, '(', ',', '=', ':', '[', '!', '&', '|', '?', '{', '}', ';' or a line start, skip a regex literal (with escapes and [...] classes) before checking for quotes.

title: The 8 MiB cap is tested only on stdin, not on the --file path
detail: openRegular has its own cap branch (`${p} is larger than 8 MiB`, src/lib/kit/slop-audit.js:648). The unit and packaged tests check oversize input only through stdin. The file branch works (probe: an 8 MiB + 1 byte file exits 1), but a regression there, such as reading the whole file before checking, would go unnoticed.
fix_hint: In the '--file relative to cwd' test, write an 8 MiB + 1 byte file and assert exit(() => run(['scan','--file','big.html'], io('', dir))).

title: One-sentence check rejects abbreviations, times and quoted periods, and prompt then exits 1
detail: The regex /[.!?]["')\]]*\s+\S/ treats any terminator followed by a space as a second sentence. Valid single sentences such as 'Mr. Lee shapes a clay bowl at a wooden bench in low morning sun.' or 'A kettle at 3 p.m. in sun on a stove.' get not-one-sentence. Probed through stdin: `sentence` reports ok:false and `prompt` refuses with exit 1 ('sentence fails the check: not-one-sentence'), so a realistic input cannot get a prompt at all. The comment says only abbreviations without a space are allowed, which leaves out the common case. No test covers it.
fix_hint: Count a terminator as a sentence break only when the next word starts with an uppercase letter and the token before it is not a known abbreviation (Mr, Mrs, Dr, St, a.m., p.m., e.g., i.e.) or a single letter. Add tests for 'Mr. Lee ...' and '3 p.m. in ...'.

title: Usage string says 'advisory, exit 0' for all three subcommands
detail: The usage text printed on every argument error says '(advisory, exit 0)'. Only the problems that `sentence` finds are advisory. `prompt` exits 1 when the sentence fails, and every subcommand exits 1 on bad input, as the header at lines 30-33 says.
fix_hint: Change it to something like '(JSON on stdin or --file; exit 0 answer, 1 bad input; sentence problems are advisory)'.

title: Style list differs from the power brief, and the banned list includes a style the brief names
detail: The power brief's style list is painted background, cinematic object, soft 3D, product object render, light and optics, engraving. STYLES is photo/illustration/render/collage, and BANNED (line 65) includes 'cinematic', which the brief names as an acceptable style. The brief says 'such as', so the list is not binding, but a reader comparing the two sees a contradiction that neither the header nor the tests explain.
fix_hint: Either line the style list up with the brief's examples, or add a line in the header saying why the set differs and why 'cinematic' is banned in the sentence but not as a style.

title: Exported functions fail badly when a code caller passes a non-object or a missing argument
detail: decide, checkSentence and buildPrompt are exported as a direct-call API, but only run() checks the input shape. Probed: decide(null) throws a raw TypeError ("Cannot use 'in' operator") instead of a KitExit. checkSentence(undefined) checks the literal string 'undefined' (line 75 String(sentence)) and returns a misleading no-concrete-subject result.
fix_hint: At the top of decide/buildPrompt, `if (!isObj(ctx)) throw bad('context must be an object')`. In checkSentence, treat a non-string as empty, or throw bad().

title: Duplicate 'cool' entry in STOP set
detail: 'cool' is listed twice in the STOP array. The Set makes the duplicate harmless, but it is a sign the list was not reviewed.
fix_hint: Remove the second 'cool'.

title: Dropping a repeated heading is not reported
detail: compare checks drops with a Set of after ids (setA.has(id)), and orderChanged only compares positions up to the length of `common`, so when a heading text appears more than once, removing one of its occurrences is invisible to both checks. Probe: before.md with `## Example`, `## Setup`, `## Example` and after.md with only the first two gives violations: [], pass: true, exit 0 even with --strict. Pages with repeated headings (several `### Example` or `## FAQ` blocks) are common in markdown specs and docs, so a dropped section passes the blocking review step.
fix_hint: Compare heading/section counts per id (a multiset): report section-dropped when after has fewer occurrences of an id than before, and add a test with a repeated heading where one copy is removed.

title: Markdown reference-style link targets are never read
detail: linkTargets for markdown only matches inline `](target)` links, so a target given as a reference definition (`[d]: https://x.y/docs`, used as `[docs][d]`) is not collected and its removal is not flagged. The header documents link-removed as covering 'an href or markdown link target'. Probe: before `See [docs][d].\n\n[d]: https://x.y/docs` and after `See docs.` returns violations: [], pass: true under check. READMEs and docs use reference links often, so a removed URL passes --strict.
fix_hint: Also collect `^ {0,3}\[[^\]]+\]:\s*<?(\S+?)>?(\s|$)` definitions (outside fences) as link targets, and add a test that removes one.

title: Template test passes when no sentence could be read
detail:
contentWords only matches ASCII `[a-z]` words, so copy in a non-Latin script yields sentences: 0, generic_ratio 0 and pass: true with the 'The copy reads as this product' next line. Probe: `

Тест

Лучшая платформа для команд.

` with --name Тест passes although nothing was checked. The 0-sentence ratio is documented, but the result claims a pass rather than saying the test could not judge the copy, and check --strict inherits it.
fix_hint: When sentences is 0, say so in next (no readable sentences, check by eye), or match words with \p{L} so non-ASCII copy is counted.

title: A failed revoke exits 1 with a generic write error and leaves any earlier confirmation in force, undocumented and untested
detail: When writeState fails for "Change the direction" (for example a missing parent dir, which a probe confirmed: `cannot write .../nope/s.json: ENOENT`, exit 1), the user's 'no' becomes exit 1, not the documented exit 2, and the message does not say the revoke failed. If an earlier confirmed record exists and the write fails (read-only dir, EISDIR), gate keeps exiting 0 with confirmed:true, and nothing in the output says so. The exit is still nonzero, so a careful caller stops, but the header (lines 16-17) promises exit 2 and says the confirmation is revoked. No test covers the revoke-failure path; the unwritable-path test only exercises the Go choice.
fix_hint: In the Change-the-direction branch, catch the write failure and rethrow KitExit(1) with text like 'could not revoke: <code>; an earlier confirmation in <path>, if any, still stands'. Note it in the header and add a test with a missing parent dir.

title: writeState cleanup deletes a temp file it did not create when wx fails with EEXIST
detail: The temp name is target.pid.Date.now().tmp. Two in-process confirm calls for the same target in the same millisecond (library use of run()) collide. The second call's writeFile with flag wx fails EEXIST, and its catch then runs fs.rm(tmp, {force:true}) on the first call's temp file, so the first call's rename fails ENOENT. Both calls report 'cannot write', and the record that should have landed is lost. Separate CLI processes are not affected, because their pids differ.
fix_hint: Only rm the temp file when writeFile succeeded (track a `created` flag), or add a random suffix (crypto.randomUUID()) to the temp name.

title: check is keyed by id alone, so it cannot confirm the prompt/model/size the step is about to send
detail: check takes only --state and --id (SPECS line 104), and exits 0 whenever that id is approved. It never sees the prompt file, model or size the workflow will pass to the image tool. A step that edits its prompt file or switches model after approval and re-runs check with the id it already holds gets exit 0 for a request the user never saw. The header (lines 30-34) does not tell the step to send exactly show.prompt/model/size either. So the gate does not prove 'approved for exactly this prompt/model/size'; it proves only 'some approved id exists'. No test covers check against a changed prompt.
fix_hint: Let check also take (or require) --prompt-file/--model/--size, recompute idOf with the same normalisation as request, and exit 2 when it differs from --id or from the stored record. At minimum, state in the header and in next that the tool must be called with exactly check's show values. Add a test where the prompt file changes after approval and check exits 2.

title: Re-request with a different --service/--est-cost/--asset silently reuses the old approval
detail: The id hashes only prompt, model and size (line 73), and request returns the stored record unchanged when the id exists (line 295). Probe: approve with --service cheap --est-cost '$0.01', then request again with --service pricey --est-cost '$5' --asset img/hero.png. The result is status approved, question null, with the old service, cost and asset in show, and check exits 0. The user agreed to one cost and one service, and a different paid run goes ahead without asking again. The caller's new --asset is also dropped without a word, so the result is saved somewhere other than the step asked.
fix_hint: When an existing record's service, est_cost or asset differs from the new flags: for a pending record, update it and re-ask; for an approved one, return status pending with a fresh question (or refuse with exit 2 and say what differs). Never return 'Already approved' for different terms. Add a test for it.

title: validateState does not tie a record's id to its content or require answered_at on approved records
detail: A state record passes validation as long as r.id equals its key and the status is known. Nothing checks that id === idOf(prompt, model, size), or that an approved record carries answered_at. A state file that was hand-edited or written by another tool, with status 'approved' or with a prompt swapped under an approved id, makes check exit 0 and show a prompt the user never approved.
fix_hint: In validateState, reject a record whose id !== idOf(r.prompt, r.model, r.size), and an approved or used record without answered_at; add a corrupt-state test for each.

title: Halftone turns transparent pixels into solid ink
detail: lum() multiplies luminance by alpha, so a fully transparent pixel reads as black. That suits glyph and dither, where dark is the background. Halftone draws dots where the picture is darker, so it fills every transparent area with full-size palette[0] dots. Rendered in Chromium with a 400x200 PNG (a white disc on a transparent background) and --palette #0b1020,#f5f0e0: the whole transparent area became a solid #0b1020 block around a light disc. A transparent-background hero (a logo, product cutout or illustration) comes out as an inverted dark rectangle.
fix_hint: For halftone, composite transparent pixels onto the paper colour (for example use lum*a + (1-a)*lum(P[1]), or fill the sample canvas with P[1] before drawImage) so transparent areas get no dots; add a rendering or unit test with an alpha pixel.

title: Glyph grid leaves out the cell animation the spec names
detail: The power brief's idea for the glyph treatment says 'only a small share of cells change at eight to twelve steps per second, paused off screen'. The module says it has 'no animation loop', and the test (canvas kinds, 'no animation loop') enforces that there is no requestAnimationFrame/setInterval/setTimeout. So the glyph kind is a static render, and nothing records a decision to drop this behaviour against the brief.
fix_hint: Add an opt-in, throttled (8-12 Hz) partial-cell redraw from the existing atlas, paused by an IntersectionObserver and switched off under prefers-reduced-motion, with a test. Or, if dropping the animation is deliberate, record that as a change to the brief and say so in list/notes.

title: --palette means a different thing for each kind; halftone silently drops the third color
detail: Dither and glyph sort the palette dark to light. Duotone and halftone use the order given. So the same --palette '#f5c542,#0b1020' gives a normal image with glyph or dither, a negative-looking duotone (the brief says brightness maps onto 'the darkest surface and the accent'), and light dots on dark paper with halftone. Halftone also accepts three colors but uses only P[0] and P[1], with no error or note. Probe: emit --kind halftone --palette '#000,#888,#fff' returns exit 0 and its notes never mention the dropped color.
fix_hint: Reject a third color for halftone (or add a note when it is ignored). Add a note when the duotone or halftone order runs light to dark, or say plainly in list/usage which kinds sort the colors.

title: Dither canvas aspect drifts from the image because the grid is rounded
detail: The dither canvas is cols x rows, with each value rounded separately from w*DPR/cell and h*DPR/cell. It is then shown at width:100%;height:auto, so the displayed height follows cols:rows instead of the image's own ratio. In Chromium a 400x200 image rendered 400x201.5 at DPR 1 and 400x199.25 at DPR 2. With a large --cell (for example 64 on a 400x150 image: 6x2 cells) the canvas shows at 400x133, a visible distortion that also shifts the layout.
fix_hint: Set the canvas's CSS aspect-ratio (or style.height) from nw/nh. Halftone already sizes from w,h.

title: --selector accepts unbalanced quotes or brackets, and --chars cannot start with '--'
detail: checkSelector only checks the character set, so 'img[alt="x]' is accepted (exit 0). The emitted CSS then has an unterminated string, which swallows the following rules, and the script's querySelectorAll throws an uncaught SyntaxError at the top level, outside the try/fallback. Separately, parse() rejects any value that starts with '--', so a plausible glyph ramp such as --chars '--==##' fails with exit 1 and '--chars needs a value'.
fix_hint: Check that quotes and brackets balance in the selector (or wrap the script's querySelectorAll in the try). Apply the '--' value check only to flags that cannot legitimately start with '-' (not --chars).

title: Header says only the first match is treated, but duotone CSS applies to every match
detail: The header says the selector 'names the image; only the first match is treated'. That holds for the canvas scripts, but the duotone CSS rule `${selector}{filter:url(#id)}` filters every element that matches. The canvas kinds' `${selector}{display:block}` rule also reaches every match.
fix_hint: Limit the 'first match only' wording to the canvas kinds, and say that duotone applies to every element the selector matches.

title: State write is atomic but not durable: no fsync before rename
detail: writeState writes the temp file and renames it over the state file without fsyncing the temp file or the folder. A crash or power loss just after confirm can leave a zero-length state file, which happens on filesystems without ext4's auto_da_alloc rename heuristic: older XFS, ext3 data=writeback, some network mounts. The next gate then exits 1 ('not valid JSON') instead of 2. Worse, a crash just after a 'Change the direction' revoke can lose the rename, so the earlier { confirmed: true } comes back and the gate passes against the user's no. The header calls the revoke a guarantee. The kit's own guarded-fs.js already fsyncs before rename.
fix_hint: Open the temp file with fs.open(tmp, 'wx'), write, await fh.sync(), close and rename. Then fsync the parent folder where that is supported (open it read-only and call sync, ignoring EISDIR/EPERM on platforms that refuse). Or reuse the guarded-fs write path.

title: Temp files left by a killed confirm are never cleaned up
detail: If the process is killed between writeFile and rename (SIGKILL, OOM, a terminal closed on a slow network mount), the uniquely named '<state>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp' file stays beside the state file for good. The catch-block cleanup only runs on a thrown error, and no later run removes such files, so they pile up in the user's folder.
fix_hint: Document the leftover pattern in the header. Or, on confirm, remove sibling '<state>.<pid>.*.tmp' files whose pid is no longer running (best effort, ignore errors).

title: TOO_MANY_SHADOWS fires on a stylesheet that only uses the sheet's own two shadow tokens
detail: The counter adds one for every box-shadow declaration that is not none/inherit/initial/unset, so three rules that each say box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm) or var(--shadow-md) count as three shadows. Probed: '.a{box-shadow:var(--shadow-sm)} .b{box-shadow:var(--shadow-md)} .c{box-shadow:var(--shadow-sm)}' gives TOO_MANY_SHADOWS at line 3, ok:false, and check --strict exits 2, with a fix text that tells the user to use --shadow-sm and --shadow-md, which they already do. Any real app that follows the emitted sheet (cards, menus, modals) puts more than two box-shadow declarations in its CSS, so the lint fails on exactly the input it is meant to approve, and in a --strict gate that is a false failure. The 'checks the emitted sheet clean' test only lints the sheet itself, never CSS that uses it. The header's 'reported at the third' declaration and the fix text's 'at most two quiet shadows' disagree on what is counted.
fix_hint: Count distinct shadow values, not declarations: normalise the value (lowercase, collapse spaces, strip !important) into a Set, skip pure var(--...) references (or count each distinct var name once), report when the Set reaches 3; update the header to say 'more than 2 distinct box-shadow values', and add a test with three rules using var(--shadow-sm)/var(--shadow-md) that stays ok.

title: box-shadow: none !important is counted as a shadow
detail: The exemption test /^(none|inherit|initial|unset)$/i runs on the raw value, so 'box-shadow: none !important' and 'box-shadow:none!important' (the common reset utility) count toward TOO_MANY_SHADOWS (probed: two such resets plus one real shadow give TOO_MANY_SHADOWS). This is the same !important gap r1 fixed for spacing; spacing and font-weight now strip it, box-shadow does not.
fix_hint: Strip a trailing \s*!important from value before the none/inherit/initial/unset test, and add a case with 'box-shadow:none!important' to the shadow test.

title: light field skips the banned-word check, so slop words reach the prompt with exit 0
detail: prompt refuses a sentence that has banned style words, but the optional light string is only checked for being a non-empty string and goes into the prompt as is. Probe: light 'stunning neon cyberpunk glow, 8k cinematic' gives exit 0 and a prompt containing 'light: stunning neon cyberpunk glow, 8k cinematic'. The power brief says to avoid glossy abstractions, and the module puts the sentence through the gate for exactly this reason, so the second free-text field undoes that gate. The same file copy is in .claude/helpers/kit/visual-direction.js.
fix_hint: Run the same BANNED match (factor it out of checkSentence) on ctx.light, and exit 1 with 'light has style words that read as slop: ...' when it hits; add a test that a banned light is rejected.

title: Any sentence in a non-Latin script fails no-concrete-subject, so prompt always exits 1
detail: The concrete-subject check removes every character outside [a-z0-9' -] before counting content words, so a Japanese or Cyrillic sentence becomes empty. Probes: '陶芸家が朝の光の中で木の作業台で粘土の鉢を形作る' and 'Плотник строгает доску на верстаке в утреннем свете.' both return ok:false with no-concrete-subject, and prompt then refuses them. Accented Latin passes only because the stripped words still leave ASCII parts. The error tells the user to 'name a real thing', which they already did, so there is no way through except rewriting in English.
fix_hint: Use Unicode classes (/[^\p{L}\p{N}' -]+/gu) for the content-word split, and for scripts without spaces skip the two-word count or count characters instead; add a non-Latin test.

title: One-sentence check still flags quoted questions and abbreviations outside the short list
detail: After the r1 fix, some single sentences are still flagged not-one-sentence, and prompt then exits 1: 'A sign reading "Open?" hangs on a wooden door in morning sun.' ('?' or '!' is not given the lowercase-next rule), 'A flag of the U.S. Navy hangs on a wall' ('u.s' is not in ABBREV) and 'A brass kettle at No. 5 on a stove' (a number after the period). These sentences are rare in visual briefs and the message tells the user how to fix it, so this is low.
fix_hint: Apply the lowercase-next skip to '?' and '!' when a closing quote follows, treat a token made of dotted single letters (u.s, u.k) as an abbreviation, and do not split when the next character is a digit.

title: No length cap on light and avoid entries, so the prompt can be megabytes
detail: The sentence is capped at 30 words, but light and each avoid entry can fill the whole 8 MiB input. Probe: a 7,000,000-character light gives exit 0 and about 7 MB of prompt JSON. An image tool would reject that or cut it short, and the user gets no warning.
fix_hint: Cap light at about 20 words and each avoid entry at about 40 characters (and the list at about 20 entries), and exit 1 with a clear message when over.

title: Unknown context keys are dropped without a message, so a typo changes the decision
detail: decide reads only the keys it knows. A misspelt key such as {screen:'dashboard', slots:'empty-state'} is dropped without a message and the answer is needed:false, kind 'none', where 'slot' would have given a visual. prompt drops misspelt keys the same way (for example headline-side or display_wdith). Nothing tells the caller the field had no effect.
fix_hint: Reject or warn on keys outside each subcommand's known set (for example an unknown_keys list in the output, or exit 1).
